paper_id: Tree-based Convolution_ A New Neural Architecture for Sentence Modeling
title: Discriminative Neural Sentence Modeling by Tree-Based Convolution
motivation: CNNs lack structural modeling; RNNs have long propagation paths causing gradient issues. Can we combine CNN efficiency with RNN structure?
problem_framing: Reformulate sentence modeling as tree-sliding convolution with max pooling to achieve short paths from any node to output
key_insight: Tree-based convolution applies fixed-depth subtree detectors sliding over parsing trees, combining structural capture with CNN-like short paths
method_signature: c-TBCNN/d-TBCNN: convolution windows over constituency/dependency trees with max pooling
evaluation_criteria: Accuracy on sentiment analysis (5-class/2-class) and 6-way question classification vs state-of-the-art baselines
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: c-TBCNN is slightly worse than d-TBCNN; 3-slot pooling for constituency trees is admitted as 'hard mechanism' temporarily; pooling effect not strong
evidence_for_taste: TBCNNs are not very sensitive to pooling methods
we regard 3-slot pooling for c-TBCNN is a hard mechanism temporarily
Further improvement can be addressed in future work
This strategy enables us to take a glance at the stability
thinking_moves: Diagnose CNN and RNN each with a specific failure mode: flatness vs long paths
Borrow max pooling from CNN but apply it on tree structure
Accept that constituency tree pooling design is imperfect
Visualize which subtree features survive pooling to validate semantic relevance
